bossPatches.summary: A six-objective fight, not six ordinary health phases: finish each Plot Armor challenge before its countdown ends to turn her next SP2 against her.

phases.name: Countdown — complete the current objective
phases.text: At the start of each Plot Armor, identify the task under the timer. Intercepts and punishes of recovery can buy time. Clear the task before the countdown ends and Gwenmaster's subsequent SP2 damages her. If time expires with the task incomplete, the same armor returns and the SP2 hurts the attacker. On a new attempt, check the displayed armor and counters rather than assuming partial task progress was saved.

phases.name: 1 · Emma Frost — build four Prowess, then Dexterity
phases.text: Use the power-bar difference to cycle Diamond Form: put your power above hers to trigger the form, then let her power move ahead to remove it and award Prowess. When four Prowess effects are showing, activate Dexterity during her SP1. Its reverse-control segment is the main execution hazard; practice the input rather than dashing by instinct.

phases.name: 2 · Killmonger — clear Counterpunch safely
phases.text: This objective is a charge-removal exercise. Repeated safe contacts reduce Counterpunch, with knockdowns taking off more. Hitting into her block can activate a short Unstoppable response; do not chase it recklessly. Her SP1 can also enable Vibranium Armor that reflects contact damage from your specials, so check the icon before attacking into it.

phases.name: 3 · Invisible Woman — strip the Force Field
phases.text: Plan several controlled intercept or special openings to earn Fury and reduce the Force Field. After Gwenmaster uses SP1, Invisibility can cause Miss. Its duration begins paused and may resume following a Miss or Bleed; let the visible state resolve rather than forcing a full combo through it. Removing the shield—not simply outlasting the timer—is the objective.

phases.name: 4 · Doctor Doom — use four different knockdowns
phases.text: Keep a checklist of Heavy, SP1, SP2 and SP3. Each must knock her down once; repeating a used method is not a substitute and can be punished by Unstoppable. She also steals power passively, so plan how to reach SP3. Be cautious after her SP1 Shock: a follow-up charged heavy can convert it into a Stun.

phases.name: 5 · Aarkus — collect Armor Breaks at range
phases.text: Create distance until ten Armor Breaks have accumulated on your attacker, then get the knockdown. Remaining too close instead feeds Gwenmaster power. Her SP1 can make approaching risky while Armor Broken because of Coldsnap, so do not rush in before a workable opening.

phases.name: 6 · Iron Man — remove the Armor Ups
phases.text: Use the fourth light attack in a combo or break her block to remove Armor Up effects. Watch the Auto-Block granted by her SP1: an appropriately timed heavy used to interrupt her heavy can clear it and remove another Armor Up. Once the armor is gone, the final objective is complete.

mistakes: Treating the encounter as a normal damage race instead of solving the current Plot Armor challenge.
Assuming partial objective counters persist after a knockout without checking the displayed state.
Trying a normal Dexterity input during Emma Frost's reversed-control SP1.
Using contact-damage specials during Killmonger's reflecting Vibranium Armor.
Repeating an already-counted knockdown in Doctor Doom's objective.
Ignoring Iron Man's Auto-Block after SP1.
bossPatches.avoid: Act 7.2.6 six-objective decision guide based on cited community descriptions. Linked nodes and specific champion interactions can change the encounter; no current-client gameplay test, rights clearance or solo guarantee is claimed.

attackerProfile: Favor a champion whose heavy and all three specials you can reliably execute; Doom's objective demands all four knockdown types.
Prioritize predictable power management and comfort reversing the Dexterity input in Emma Frost's challenge.
A familiar attacker and clean objective execution matter more here than assuming one specific champion is a universal solution.

preparation: Read the linked quest node and current in-game objective text before starting; this guide does not cover every linked-path modifier.
Choose an attacker with predictable power generation and a usable Heavy, SP1, SP2 and SP3. This is an execution checklist, not a ranked counter list.
Prepare for reverse controls, Miss, reflection and Auto-Block across different objectives; reassess when Plot Armor changes.

troubleshooting.problem: Her SP2 damages me and the same objective returns
troubleshooting.response: The countdown likely expired before the current Plot Armor was cleared. Check the active condition first; stall the timer with safe interrupts rather than treating ordinary damage as progress.

troubleshooting.problem: I can't clear Emma Frost's challenge
troubleshooting.response: Count four Prowess effects from cycling the power-bar relationship. Then activate Dexterity during her SP1 with the reversed controls in mind.

troubleshooting.problem: My specials hit into damage reflection
troubleshooting.response: Check whether Killmonger's Vibranium Armor is active after SP1. Avoid contact-damage specials while that effect is present.

troubleshooting.problem: The Invisible Woman objective seems stuck
troubleshooting.response: Look for the Force Field and Invisibility effects separately. Avoid repeatedly missing into Invisibility; return to safe intercept/special openings when you can hit.
Track all four distinct methods and whether the knockdown connected. Repeating a method does not satisfy a missing one; account for passive power steal.
After SP1, seek a safe heavy-versus-heavy interruption to remove Auto-Block, or continue with a valid armor-removal method when the opening is available.

bossPatches.summary: Solve the Power Loop prompts to open Time Collapse damage windows. Before entering, check the linked path: some Paradox nodes impose separate conditions for dealing damage.

phases.name: Power Loop — match the prompt, not a fixed rotation
phases.text: When Kang shows a number from zero to three, plan around that many full bars of your own power at countdown expiry. For a nonzero prompt, a matching special that knocks him down can complete it early; zero instead requires holding below one full bar until the timer resolves. A heavy can pause the loop, buying time to adjust your meter. Successful prompts add Power Charges; do not confuse them with path-specific Paradox charges.

phases.name: Control power with his specials
phases.text: His SP1 is useful for steering your meter: dodging its hits can give you power, while blocking drains it. Do not dodge every hit automatically when the next prompt asks for zero or one bar. Avoid SP2 contact even through block because it can apply Power Lock and Special Lock, disrupting the next loop.

phases.name: 100–91% — earn three Power Charges
phases.text: Three successful Power Loop prompts open Time Collapse, the window when the boss's damage reduction falls and your damage matters. Save reliable bursts for that period. On phase transition Kang becomes temporarily Indestructible and later rushes aggressively while Unblockable; stop your rotation and evade instead of forcing damage. Both power meters reset.

phases.name: 90–51% — earn four Power Charges
phases.text: The next Time Collapse requires four charges. Passive power gain and cheaper specials alter the timing of each number prompt, so check your meter after every special. Once Time Collapse begins, prioritize usable damage before the brief opening ends.

phases.name: 50–2% — earn six Power Charges
phases.text: This stretch needs six charges while passive power drain makes storing a requested bar harder. Repeating the same combo-ending attack also drains power. Vary your endings and use the heavy pause or SP1 block/dodge choices deliberately rather than reacting to the prompt too late.

phases.name: Final 2% — launch SP3 before Kang
phases.text: When he reaches the finish, ordinary hits and lower specials no longer damage him. Both power meters reset, Kang is Unblockable, and staying closer increases your power gain. Manage spacing and build your SP3 before his lethal SP3; this is a separate finishing race, not another Power Loop prompt.

mistakes: Using the 7.4.6 Superior Kang Slipstream strategy for the different 7.3.6 Tech Kang fight.
Using the right special without actually knocking Kang down on a nonzero Power Loop prompt.
Trying to solve a zero-bar prompt with a special instead of managing the power meter until expiry.
Dodging every SP1 hit even when the current power target is low.
Forcing damage into the Indestructible transition or forgetting the power reset.
Assuming Time Collapse alone bypasses additional Paradox-linked damage reduction on every path.
bossPatches.avoid: The base Power Loop is not the only possible restriction. Some linked routes use Neuro-Kinetic Paradox conditions that can cause little or no damage despite correct Power Charges; review the exact route and its eligible class/buff or Paradox requirements. Historical ability-accuracy reports describe issues, but they are not proof of a current bug or a reason to skip the prompt. No current-client solo test is recorded.

attackerProfile: Choose a champion with controllable power and specials that reliably knock down; fast or passive power gain may help or hinder different numbers.
Practice using SP1 dodge-versus-block choices to adjust power; avoiding SP2 remains the safer starting approach.
For Paradox-linked paths, confirm that your chosen attacker and carried path effects meet that path's separate damage condition before committing to the boss.

cheatSheet.objective: Build and land SP3 before Kang

cheatSheet.watch: Time Collapse does not replace path-specific conditions

preparation: Confirm you selected Kang the Conqueror in story 7.3.6—not Superior Kang from 7.4.6.
Read all linked nodes before leaving the path. Some Paradox-linked routes demand specific charges, class combinations or effects before normal Time Collapse damage works.
Pick an attacker whose specials can score knockdowns and whose power meter you can steer. Remember that phase transitions reset power.

troubleshooting.problem: I perform the right special but don't receive a charge
troubleshooting.response: Make sure the nonzero prompt matches the special and that its hit actually knocked Kang down. For zero, wait until the timer ends while holding below one bar. Historical reports mention ability-accuracy interactions, but they do not establish a current bug.

troubleshooting.problem: I enter Time Collapse but deal zero damage
troubleshooting.response: First review the path rather than assuming the Power Loop failed. Some Paradox-linked node combinations add extra damage-reduction conditions involving class, buffs or charges. Consult your exact node text before spending more revives.

troubleshooting.problem: I keep overshooting the power target
troubleshooting.response: SP1 offers a power-control choice: successful dodges add power while blocked hits drain it. In later phases, passive gain, reduced special costs or drain can change your usual timing.

troubleshooting.problem: Kang stops taking damage and turns aggressive
troubleshooting.response: Check whether you triggered a phase transition. He becomes temporarily Indestructible and later rushes Unblockable; back off, avoid the rush and rebuild power after the reset.
The finish requires SP3, not another Time Collapse. Build power by managing distance during his Unblockable phase and launch yours before his lethal SP3.
